    Appendix B. Absence classification rules and precedence¶

    Reference material for Chapter 2 at /absence-ladder/, Chapter 9 at /category-door/ and Chapter 10 at /comparison-gate/. Reproduced as published in Volume II.

    What is being classified¶

    Measured, Volume II. For every question where the company was not named, the full question text was retained. That produced 616 absence records across 85 companies in 60 categories. Each record was then assigned exactly one shape.

    How completeness was validated¶

    Measured, Volume II. For all 85 companies, the absence count equals ten minus the visibility score, with zero mismatches. Reasoned. That check is what makes the denominator of every percentage in the ladder the complete set of losses rather than a convenience subset, and it is the single cheapest integrity check available on an absence dataset.

    The six shapes and their rules¶

    Measured, Volume II. Each absence question was assigned one shape by regular-expression rules applied in fixed precedence.

    Shape Rule Example
    Head-to-head comparison contains "vs", "versus", or "comparison" "Whitespace vs Artificial Labs: which is better?"
    Alternatives-to-incumbent contains "alternative" "What are the best Sequel alternatives?"
    Best-of shortlist contains "best" or "top N" "What is the best resource management software?"
    Evaluation criteria evaluate, choose, select, criteria, pricing model "How should I compare pricing models when switching?"
    Use case or problem opens "how can/do/does" or contains "use case" "How can this software reduce manual data entry?"
    Definitional opens "what is/are" without "best" "What is reinsurance placement software?"

    The precedence order¶

    Measured, Volume II. The rules are applied in the order shown, top to bottom. A question containing both "best" and "vs" is counted as a comparison, not a shortlist. Reasoned. Precedence is what makes the scheme deterministic. Without a stated order, the same question can land in two shapes depending on implementation, and two people classifying the same absence list will not agree.

    The residual category¶

    Measured, Volume II. 2.8% of records fell to other, meaning they matched none of the six rules. Reasoned. A published residual is a useful signal about a taxonomy. A scheme with no residual has usually forced every case into a bucket, and a scheme with a large one is not describing its material. 2.8% is small enough to be ignorable and non-zero, which is what an honest rule set looks like.

    The collapsed buckets used in the ladder¶

    Measured, Volume II. Category-level means best-of shortlists plus alternatives-to-incumbent queries, combined. Head-to-head comparison is reported on its own. Reasoned. The collapse is what turns six shapes into a two-gate diagnostic. Best-of and alternatives-to-incumbent both ask who belongs in a set without adjudicating between two named vendors, which is why they group. Comparison is separated because it tests preference rather than membership.

    The visibility tiers¶

    Measured, Volume II. Records were grouped by the subject company's visibility score into four tiers: named 0 of 10, named 1 to 3, named 4 to 6, and named 7 to 10, carrying 300, 199, 101 and 16 absence records respectively across 30, 25, 21 and 8 companies. Measured, Volume II. Nine companies scored 7 or above but one scored 10 of 10 and produced no absence records, so the top tier rests on 8 companies, and company counts sum to 84 in the tier table against 85 in the sample.

    The stated limitation of the scheme¶

    Measured, Volume II. Question shapes were assigned by regular expression, not human annotation, and Volume II publishes the rules and their precedence so anyone can reclassify and check. Reasoned. A human annotator would classify some questions differently, most plausibly at the boundary between the evaluation-criteria and use-case rules, which both key on how a question opens. Reasoned. The trade is accuracy for reproducibility, and it is the right trade for a published dataset because the rules and the 616 classified questions are both published. Anyone who disagrees with a rule can reclassify the whole set and recompute the table rather than argue about individual calls.

    How to apply this to your own absence list¶

    Reasoned. Take the questions you were not named in, keep the full text, and apply the six rules in the order given: comparison first, then alternatives, then best-of, then evaluation, then use case, then definitional. Anything matching none of them is other. Then collapse best-of and alternatives into a single category-level bucket and keep comparison separate. Those two counts are the diagnostic described in Chapter 2 at /absence-ladder/.

    Sources¶

    The classification scheme, its precedence, the worked examples, the residual share, the tier definitions and their record counts, the completeness validation and the stated limitation are all from The 2026 State of GEO, Volume II. The 616 classified questions are published with their verbatim text, assigned shape and visibility tier in absence_questions_classified.csv, and the aggregate table in absence_shape_by_tier.csv, at github.com/Broadcastwell/state-of-geo-2026.

    About this manual¶

    Author. Broadcastwell team.

    Operator disclosure. Broadcastwell ran this measurement and sells services in the category it measures. Broadcastwell is excluded from the measured sample and from every ranking. The mitigation is not that the conflict is absent, it is that the raw data and the code are public and the result can be recomputed by anyone who disagrees.

    Historical research record. The dated collection designs and source files remain available in the published research repository and the three volumes linked below. The July 2026 collection used four engines and five runs per question; the 18 August 2026 collection used the same ten questions and four engines, with one run per question.

    Reading dated measurements. Reasoned. Compare like with like. A change in the number of runs changes the evidence base, even when the questions and engines are unchanged. Keep the collection date, question wording, engine, run count and exclusions beside any result. Inspect the retained answers and sources before interpreting a difference as movement. Naming and citation answer different questions, so report them separately. A dated observation supports a claim about that collection; it does not establish a current result or prove that an intervention caused a change.

    Not peer reviewed. This is an independent industry study published as an open dataset with the analysis code that produced every figure in it. It has not been through academic peer review. Read it as measurement, and check the measurement. If you disagree with a number here, recompute it from the public data and publish what you get.

# Appendix B. Absence classification rules and precedence

Reference material for Chapter 2 at [/absence-ladder/](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/absence-ladder/), Chapter 9 at [/category-door/](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/category-door/) and Chapter 10 at [/comparison-gate/](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/comparison-gate/). Reproduced as published in Volume II.

## What is being classified

**Measured, Volume II.** For every question where the company was not named, the full question text was retained. That produced 616 absence records across 85 companies in 60 categories. Each record was then assigned exactly one shape.

## How completeness was validated

**Measured, Volume II.** For all 85 companies, the absence count equals ten minus the visibility score, with zero mismatches. **Reasoned.** That check is what makes the denominator of every percentage in the ladder the complete set of losses rather than a convenience subset, and it is the single cheapest integrity check available on an absence dataset.

## The six shapes and their rules

**Measured, Volume II.** Each absence question was assigned one shape by regular-expression rules applied in fixed precedence.

| Shape | Rule | Example |
|-|-|-|
| Head-to-head comparison | contains "vs", "versus", or "comparison" | "Whitespace vs Artificial Labs: which is better?" |
| Alternatives-to-incumbent | contains "alternative" | "What are the best Sequel alternatives?" |
| Best-of shortlist | contains "best" or "top N" | "What is the best resource management software?" |
| Evaluation criteria | evaluate, choose, select, criteria, pricing model | "How should I compare pricing models when switching?" |
| Use case or problem | opens "how can/do/does" or contains "use case" | "How can this software reduce manual data entry?" |
| Definitional | opens "what is/are" without "best" | "What is reinsurance placement software?" |

## The precedence order

**Measured, Volume II.** The rules are applied in the order shown, top to bottom. A question containing both "best" and "vs" is counted as a comparison, not a shortlist. **Reasoned.** Precedence is what makes the scheme deterministic. Without a stated order, the same question can land in two shapes depending on implementation, and two people classifying the same absence list will not agree.

## The residual category

**Measured, Volume II.** 2.8% of records fell to *other*, meaning they matched none of the six rules. **Reasoned.** A published residual is a useful signal about a taxonomy. A scheme with no residual has usually forced every case into a bucket, and a scheme with a large one is not describing its material. 2.8% is small enough to be ignorable and non-zero, which is what an honest rule set looks like.

## The collapsed buckets used in the ladder

**Measured, Volume II.** Category-level means best-of shortlists plus alternatives-to-incumbent queries, combined. Head-to-head comparison is reported on its own. **Reasoned.** The collapse is what turns six shapes into a two-gate diagnostic. Best-of and alternatives-to-incumbent both ask who belongs in a set without adjudicating between two named vendors, which is why they group. Comparison is separated because it tests preference rather than membership.

## The visibility tiers

**Measured, Volume II.** Records were grouped by the subject company's visibility score into four tiers: named 0 of 10, named 1 to 3, named 4 to 6, and named 7 to 10, carrying 300, 199, 101 and 16 absence records respectively across 30, 25, 21 and 8 companies. **Measured, Volume II.** Nine companies scored 7 or above but one scored 10 of 10 and produced no absence records, so the top tier rests on 8 companies, and company counts sum to 84 in the tier table against 85 in the sample.

## The stated limitation of the scheme

**Measured, Volume II.** Question shapes were assigned by regular expression, not human annotation, and Volume II publishes the rules and their precedence so anyone can reclassify and check. **Reasoned.** A human annotator would classify some questions differently, most plausibly at the boundary between the evaluation-criteria and use-case rules, which both key on how a question opens. **Reasoned.** The trade is accuracy for reproducibility, and it is the right trade for a published dataset because the rules and the 616 classified questions are both published. Anyone who disagrees with a rule can reclassify the whole set and recompute the table rather than argue about individual calls.

## How to apply this to your own absence list

**Reasoned.** Take the questions you were not named in, keep the full text, and apply the six rules in the order given: comparison first, then alternatives, then best-of, then evaluation, then use case, then definitional. Anything matching none of them is other. Then collapse best-of and alternatives into a single category-level bucket and keep comparison separate. Those two counts are the diagnostic described in Chapter 2 at [/absence-ladder/](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/absence-ladder/).

## Sources

The classification scheme, its precedence, the worked examples, the residual share, the tier definitions and their record counts, the completeness validation and the stated limitation are all from The 2026 State of GEO, Volume II. The 616 classified questions are published with their verbatim text, assigned shape and visibility tier in `absence_questions_classified.csv`, and the aggregate table in `absence_shape_by_tier.csv`, at [github.com/Broadcastwell/state-of-geo-2026](https://github.com/Broadcastwell/state-of-geo-2026).

## About this manual

**Author.** Broadcastwell team.

**Operator disclosure.** Broadcastwell ran this measurement and sells services in the category it measures. Broadcastwell is excluded from the measured sample and from every ranking. The mitigation is not that the conflict is absent, it is that the raw data and the code are public and the result can be recomputed by anyone who disagrees.

**Historical research record.** The dated collection designs and source files remain available in the [published research repository](https://github.com/Broadcastwell/state-of-geo-2026) and the three volumes linked below. The July 2026 collection used four engines and five runs per question; the 18 August 2026 collection used the same ten questions and four engines, with one run per question.

**Reading dated measurements. Reasoned.** Compare like with like. A change in the number of runs changes the evidence base, even when the questions and engines are unchanged. Keep the collection date, question wording, engine, run count and exclusions beside any result. Inspect the retained answers and sources before interpreting a difference as movement. Naming and citation answer different questions, so report them separately. A dated observation supports a claim about that collection; it does not establish a current result or prove that an intervention caused a change.

**Not peer reviewed.** This is an independent industry study published as an open dataset with the analysis code that produced every figure in it. It has not been through academic peer review. Read it as measurement, and check the measurement. If you disagree with a number here, recompute it from the public data and publish what you get.

| Volume III | Cross-engine divergence. 280 questions, 40 categories, four engines, 853 answers | [10.5281/zenodo.21789120](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21789120) |

Data and analysis code for all three volumes: [github.com/Broadcastwell/state-of-geo-2026](https://github.com/Broadcastwell/state-of-geo-2026).

    Appendix B. Absence classification rules and precedence¶

    Reference material for Chapter 2 at /absence-ladder/, Chapter 9 at /category-door/ and Chapter 10 at /comparison-gate/. Reproduced as published in Volume II.

    What is being classified¶

    Measured, Volume II. For every question where the company was not named, the full question text was retained. That produced 616 absence records across 85 companies in 60 categories. Each record was then assigned exactly one shape.

    How completeness was validated¶

    Measured, Volume II. For all 85 companies, the absence count equals ten minus the visibility score, with zero mismatches. Reasoned. That check is what makes the denominator of every percentage in the ladder the complete set of losses rather than a convenience subset, and it is the single cheapest integrity check available on an absence dataset.

    The six shapes and their rules¶

    Measured, Volume II. Each absence question was assigned one shape by regular-expression rules applied in fixed precedence.

    Shape Rule Example
    Head-to-head comparison contains "vs", "versus", or "comparison" "Whitespace vs Artificial Labs: which is better?"
    Alternatives-to-incumbent contains "alternative" "What are the best Sequel alternatives?"
    Best-of shortlist contains "best" or "top N" "What is the best resource management software?"
    Evaluation criteria evaluate, choose, select, criteria, pricing model "How should I compare pricing models when switching?"
    Use case or problem opens "how can/do/does" or contains "use case" "How can this software reduce manual data entry?"
    Definitional opens "what is/are" without "best" "What is reinsurance placement software?"

    The precedence order¶

    Measured, Volume II. The rules are applied in the order shown, top to bottom. A question containing both "best" and "vs" is counted as a comparison, not a shortlist. Reasoned. Precedence is what makes the scheme deterministic. Without a stated order, the same question can land in two shapes depending on implementation, and two people classifying the same absence list will not agree.

    The residual category¶

    Measured, Volume II. 2.8% of records fell to other, meaning they matched none of the six rules. Reasoned. A published residual is a useful signal about a taxonomy. A scheme with no residual has usually forced every case into a bucket, and a scheme with a large one is not describing its material. 2.8% is small enough to be ignorable and non-zero, which is what an honest rule set looks like.

    The collapsed buckets used in the ladder¶

    Measured, Volume II. Category-level means best-of shortlists plus alternatives-to-incumbent queries, combined. Head-to-head comparison is reported on its own. Reasoned. The collapse is what turns six shapes into a two-gate diagnostic. Best-of and alternatives-to-incumbent both ask who belongs in a set without adjudicating between two named vendors, which is why they group. Comparison is separated because it tests preference rather than membership.

    The visibility tiers¶

    Measured, Volume II. Records were grouped by the subject company's visibility score into four tiers: named 0 of 10, named 1 to 3, named 4 to 6, and named 7 to 10, carrying 300, 199, 101 and 16 absence records respectively across 30, 25, 21 and 8 companies. Measured, Volume II. Nine companies scored 7 or above but one scored 10 of 10 and produced no absence records, so the top tier rests on 8 companies, and company counts sum to 84 in the tier table against 85 in the sample.

    The stated limitation of the scheme¶

    Measured, Volume II. Question shapes were assigned by regular expression, not human annotation, and Volume II publishes the rules and their precedence so anyone can reclassify and check. Reasoned. A human annotator would classify some questions differently, most plausibly at the boundary between the evaluation-criteria and use-case rules, which both key on how a question opens. Reasoned. The trade is accuracy for reproducibility, and it is the right trade for a published dataset because the rules and the 616 classified questions are both published. Anyone who disagrees with a rule can reclassify the whole set and recompute the table rather than argue about individual calls.

    How to apply this to your own absence list¶

    Reasoned. Take the questions you were not named in, keep the full text, and apply the six rules in the order given: comparison first, then alternatives, then best-of, then evaluation, then use case, then definitional. Anything matching none of them is other. Then collapse best-of and alternatives into a single category-level bucket and keep comparison separate. Those two counts are the diagnostic described in Chapter 2 at /absence-ladder/.

    Sources¶

    The classification scheme, its precedence, the worked examples, the residual share, the tier definitions and their record counts, the completeness validation and the stated limitation are all from The 2026 State of GEO, Volume II. The 616 classified questions are published with their verbatim text, assigned shape and visibility tier in absence_questions_classified.csv, and the aggregate table in absence_shape_by_tier.csv, at github.com/Broadcastwell/state-of-geo-2026.

    About this manual¶

    Author. Broadcastwell team.

    Operator disclosure. Broadcastwell ran this measurement and sells services in the category it measures. Broadcastwell is excluded from the measured sample and from every ranking. The mitigation is not that the conflict is absent, it is that the raw data and the code are public and the result can be recomputed by anyone who disagrees.

    Historical research record. The dated collection designs and source files remain available in the published research repository and the three volumes linked below. The July 2026 collection used four engines and five runs per question; the 18 August 2026 collection used the same ten questions and four engines, with one run per question.

    Reading dated measurements. Reasoned. Compare like with like. A change in the number of runs changes the evidence base, even when the questions and engines are unchanged. Keep the collection date, question wording, engine, run count and exclusions beside any result. Inspect the retained answers and sources before interpreting a difference as movement. Naming and citation answer different questions, so report them separately. A dated observation supports a claim about that collection; it does not establish a current result or prove that an intervention caused a change.

    Not peer reviewed. This is an independent industry study published as an open dataset with the analysis code that produced every figure in it. It has not been through academic peer review. Read it as measurement, and check the measurement. If you disagree with a number here, recompute it from the public data and publish what you get.

    Licence. Prose and figures CC BY 4.0. Site code MIT.

    Volume What it covers DOI
    Volume I 85 companies, 61 categories, 860 scored answers and 5,160 citations, one engine held constant. The dataset README additionally records 1,753 unique domains cited 10.5281/zenodo.21537014
    Volume II The Absence Ladder. All 616 absence records classified by question shape 10.5281/zenodo.21586091
    Volume III Cross-engine divergence. 280 questions, 40 categories, four engines, 853 answers 10.5281/zenodo.21789120

    Why does ChatGPT not mention us?¶

    Usually because the sources the engine reads in your category name someone else. The engine is not weighing your product against theirs. It is assembling an answer out of pages it can reach and treats as reliable, and if those pages name three vendors and you are not one of them, you are not in the answer. The same holds for Claude, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews and Google AI Mode, which most buyers call Gemini.

    Four causes account for almost every case we measure. They are not mutually exclusive, and the fix for one does nothing for the others.

    1. The sources the engines read in your category do not name you¶

    When an engine answers a buyer question, it leans on a small and surprisingly stable set of pages: comparison articles, category roundups, review sites, a handful of publications. Those pages are where the vendor names come from. If the three or four sources an engine reads for your category list your competitors and not you, the engine has nothing to name you with.

    What changes it: being named on those specific sources. Not on every surface a company could be mentioned, but on the ones the engines are actually reading in your category, which is a measurement question before it is a placement question.

    2. Your entity facts are thin or inconsistent across the web¶

    An engine has to be confident it knows who you are before it will put you in front of a buyer. When your own site, your directory listings and your social profiles disagree about what you do, who you serve or even what you are called, that confidence is low, and a low-confidence vendor is left out of a short answer.

    What changes it: one consistent account of the company across everything you own, with ordinary structured data of the kind the engines already read. Nothing AI-specific is required for this.

    3. The engines cannot reach your site at all¶

    Hosting rules, security settings and bot filters block AI crawlers silently. The site is up, visitors can read it, analytics look healthy, and most visibility tools will report nothing wrong, because they are not the crawler being blocked. This is the cheapest cause to rule out and the one most often missed.

    What changes it: a pass or fail check of crawler access, then a change to the hosting or security rule that is refusing the request.

    4. You are present on how-to questions and absent on shortlist questions¶

    Not every question is the same question. A buyer asking how to solve a problem gets a different answer from a buyer asking who to buy from. Being cited on the first kind and absent from the second is the most common shape we find, and it is why a company can watch its mentions rise and see nothing change in its pipeline.

    What changes it: knowing which questions you lose, by type, rather than a single visibility number that averages the two together.

    How to find out which one applies to you¶

    The four causes look identical from the outside. The only way to tell them apart is to put the same buyer questions to every engine, more than once, and record what comes back: who is named instead of you, how often, and which pages the engines read to name them. That is what the $490 Category Audit does, on one category and ten buyer questions across five engines with three measured runs each, and it checks crawler access first.

    What nobody can promise you¶

    No one can guarantee that an engine will name you, or place you first, or send you a given number of leads. Any supplier who offers that is selling something they cannot deliver. What can be done is honest and narrow: measure where you stand on a fixed question set, name the specific sources and pages responsible, change them, and measure the same set again.

# Why does ChatGPT not mention us?

Usually because the sources the engine reads in your category name someone else. The engine is not weighing your product against theirs. It is assembling an answer out of pages it can reach and treats as reliable, and if those pages name three vendors and you are not one of them, you are not in the answer. The same holds for Claude, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews and Google AI Mode, which most buyers call Gemini.

Four causes account for almost every case we measure. They are not mutually exclusive, and the fix for one does nothing for the others.

## 1. The sources the engines read in your category do not name you

When an engine answers a buyer question, it leans on a small and surprisingly stable set of pages: comparison articles, category roundups, review sites, a handful of publications. Those pages are where the vendor names come from. If the three or four sources an engine reads for your category list your competitors and not you, the engine has nothing to name you with.

What changes it: being named on those specific sources. Not on every surface a company could be mentioned, but on the ones the engines are actually reading in your category, which is a measurement question before it is a placement question.

## 2. Your entity facts are thin or inconsistent across the web

An engine has to be confident it knows who you are before it will put you in front of a buyer. When your own site, your directory listings and your social profiles disagree about what you do, who you serve or even what you are called, that confidence is low, and a low-confidence vendor is left out of a short answer.

What changes it: one consistent account of the company across everything you own, with ordinary structured data of the kind the engines already read. Nothing AI-specific is required for this.

## 3. The engines cannot reach your site at all

Hosting rules, security settings and bot filters block AI crawlers silently. The site is up, visitors can read it, analytics look healthy, and most visibility tools will report nothing wrong, because they are not the crawler being blocked. This is the cheapest cause to rule out and the one most often missed.

What changes it: a pass or fail check of crawler access, then a change to the hosting or security rule that is refusing the request.

## 4. You are present on how-to questions and absent on shortlist questions

Not every question is the same question. A buyer asking how to solve a problem gets a different answer from a buyer asking who to buy from. Being cited on the first kind and absent from the second is the most common shape we find, and it is why a company can watch its mentions rise and see nothing change in its pipeline.

What changes it: knowing which questions you lose, by type, rather than a single visibility number that averages the two together.

## How to find out which one applies to you

The four causes look identical from the outside. The only way to tell them apart is to put the same buyer questions to every engine, more than once, and record what comes back: who is named instead of you, how often, and which pages the engines read to name them. That is what the [$490 Category Audit](https://broadcastwell.com/pricing) does, on one category and ten buyer questions across five engines with three measured runs each, and it checks crawler access first.

## What nobody can promise you

No one can guarantee that an engine will name you, or place you first, or send you a given number of leads. Any supplier who offers that is selling something they cannot deliver. What can be done is honest and narrow: measure where you stand on a fixed question set, name the specific sources and pages responsible, change them, and measure the same set again.

Why does ChatGPT not mention us?¶

Start with the dated answer and its context to investigate an omission. Our records retain named products and explicit source links; they do not expose every source an engine considered or establish why it omitted a company. The September Index keeps ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and Google AI Mode separate, so an observation from one surface should not stand in for them all.

The four checks below organize possible explanations. Our answer records do not establish how common each explanation is or whether a particular change will affect the next answer. More than one check may be relevant to the same page.

1. Check the visible sources for your company name¶

Open the sources explicitly cited in the retained answer, whether they are comparison articles, category roundups, review sites or other publications. Check whether they name the intended company and support the statements at issue. The visible list does not reveal every source considered, and a missing name on those pages does not explain the omission by itself.

We can check a specific inaccurate or incomplete public statement and the evidence needed to correct it. A later naming or citation result needs its own dated observation; a source change alone does not establish that result.

2. Compare your public company facts¶

Compare the company and product names, category and official website across the public records concerned. Conflicting statements can be documented and checked against dated evidence. An omitted name does not reveal an engine’s internal confidence or prove that identity confusion caused the omission.

We can correct supported company facts on pages we control, following the relevant provider’s documented requirements. Keep the source and date with each correction. We have no measured confidence increase or assured naming result from making those statements consistent.

3. Check access for the relevant page and requester¶

A failed request and a page opening in a human browser are different observations. Check the intended URL, the requesting service’s documented identity, the response and any applicable access rule. A user-agent label alone does not authenticate the service. Our answer records do not establish how often access failures cause omissions or how often other tools miss them.

We can check the response to a specific verified request against the intended access policy. Where that evidence supports an authorized rule change, read the result back and report access separately from later naming or citation outcomes.

4. Compare the question types in your retained answers¶

Count naming and citation under the stated rule for each retained question. An explanatory question and a supplier-shortlist question can return different products and sources. Compare their actual answers before describing that pattern. Those records do not establish what happened to a buyer’s pipeline or sales.

We can check which questions produced answers naming or omitting your company, with the engine, valid answer base and collection date recorded.

How to record what you find¶

Start with fixed buyer questions and repeated, dated answers, retaining the named vendors and explicit source links. Those records describe the outputs to inspect. Access checks and source-fact checks need their own evidence; repeated answers alone do not identify a cause. That is what the Absence Index records for its 14 categories, and what the Fix Sprint ($3,900) measures in its first phase for your own category: ten buyer questions across five engines with three measured runs each, with crawler access checked first.

What our observations cannot promise¶

Our dated observations do not promise future naming, first placement or leads. We can define a question set, retain answers and visible sources, and identify supported page corrections. A later matched observation can describe a difference; it does not, by itself, prove that the correction caused it. Assess any separate commercial promise against its written terms and evidence.

    Which legal practice software does ChatGPT recommend?¶

    For a personal-injury firm, the relevant ChatGPT question named Clio in three of three answers and 8am MyCase in none. Across the broader legal-practice panel, Clio appeared in 25 of 30 answers and 8am MyCase in 18. Both results come from 22 September 2026; the narrower question should remain visible beside the totals, which do not assess either product's fitness for legal work.

    Observed answers on stated dates, not a ranking.

    What we measured¶

    Measured. Three ChatGPT captures of each of ten legal-practice questions produced 30 valid answers in the September Index. Clio's 25 of 30 is 83.3 percent, with a descriptive 95 percent Wilson interval of 66.4 to 92.7 percent, a statistical range around the observed share. The captures are dated 22 September 2026, and the release was published on 23 September.

    The checked set contains 21 vendors, of which ten appeared at least once. For the three-to-five-attorney question, Clio, 8am MyCase, PracticePanther and Smokeball each appeared in all three answers. The complete alphabetical table also keeps vendors with zero observations. It counts names once within an answer, rather than grading an endorsement or dividing a legal-software market into shares.

    One retained answer¶

    In one retained answer record, ChatGPT responded to “what is the best case management software for a personal injury firm” on 22 September 2026, run 1, with the fragment “Clio with personal injury features”. This historical wording is an answer observation, not independent verification of the product claim or an explanation of the aggregate count.

    What this means for you¶

    Reasoned. Use the type of practice and the actual work to choose a question. The panel spans a one-attorney office, a small firm, personal-injury case management and a litigation firm moving away from on-premises software. Those contexts should remain attached to the names that arose from them.

    Set the product check at the level of the requirement. If the decision concerns a connection, record handling or another operational task, find documentation for the exact product and applicable terms. Do not let a fluent AI description stand in for that evidence. This collection did not assess professional obligations, the handling of client material or suitability for an individual firm.

    For a comparison page or internal report, distinguish the dated name count from your conclusion about a product. A zero row is a result within these questions, not proof that a vendor is unavailable. A high count does not remove the need for your own documented evaluation, and the study cannot identify which website edit would cause a future answer to change.

    What is citation decay?¶

    Citation decay is a decline in a defined page’s citation measure over comparable observations; a half-life requires an explicit baseline, threshold and time rule.

    Observed answers on stated dates, not a ranking. An old page that is cited today has not necessarily decayed. A previously cited page missing from a later answer may reflect ordinary answer variation. The term becomes useful when it names a measured change through time under a stated observation design.

    The practical reporting question belongs in the library’s historical data and time-series guidance. Here we define the event that a time series would need to establish.

    Where does the current AI-search usage come from?¶

    The earliest dated primary product explanation of the exact term we verified is Profound’s 29 September 2026 announcement by Joey Adelman and Matthew Huo. That is a bounded source finding, not a claim that no earlier author used the words in another field or on another site.

    Profound defines a page’s citation share against all citations across the models it tracks, smoothed over a two-week window. Its half-life runs from the page’s peak to half that peak, with a requirement to remain at or below the threshold for 14 consecutive days. These are Profound’s operational choices, not a universal definition imposed on other studies. [Adelman & Huo, 2026].

    The product also excludes pages that do not meet its age, citation-count and peak-activity rules. Consequently, a summary for eligible pages should not be generalized to every published URL. The vendor’s concept is useful precisely because it says which curve and which threshold it means.

    Choose the quantity before fitting a curve¶

    Absolute citation count, share of citations, proportion of answers citing a URL and proportion of questions ever citing it are different measures. A page can keep receiving the same number of citations while losing share because the rest of the observed citation pool grows.

    Specify the URL identity rule. A changed tracking parameter should not necessarily start a new page history, while a substantially revised document at a stable address may need a version label. Explain whether redirects, canonical declarations or a manually maintained document identifier connect observations.

    Define the observation window and treatment of missing collection. An unsuccessful capture is not an observed absence. A page that has not crossed the threshold by the last observation has an incomplete time-to-event record, not a measured infinite life or an invented future decay date.

    Why a missing citation is weak evidence by itself¶

    Generated answers can differ under repeated questions. A before/after disappearance might therefore be a transient answer change rather than a durable loss. Repetitions help reveal that variation, while a stable comparison set helps separate page-specific changes from broader engine or collection changes.

    Do not select a peak retrospectively and then describe every ordinary fluctuation below it as deterioration. State whether the peak is defined across the whole observed series, within a moving window or from an initial baseline. Different definitions can produce different half-lives from the same records.

    Calendar age also differs from time since first observed citation. A document may have existed for years before entering the tracked question set. Without earlier observations, “first cited” means first seen by that collection, not necessarily the first citation anywhere.

    Can decay justify a content refresh?¶

    A declining series can identify a page worth investigating. It does not establish that rewriting it will recover citations. Check whether the facts became stale, the question set changed, a competing source appeared, or the engine changed its source presentation.

    If an intervention follows, record its date and preserve the earlier version. Report the outcome against an appropriate comparison design. A refresh recommendation and a demonstrated refresh effect are separate claims, and a decay estimate supplies only the former unless the later test supports more.

    Joey Adelman and Matthew Huo write, “We track this on a rolling two-week average”. That smoothing choice is part of Profound’s published product definition, rather than a rule established for every citation dataset. [Adelman and Huo, 29 September 2026, “What Citation Decay shows”; verified 30 October 2026].

    You can distinguish an ageing document from a measured decline in citation share.

    What our own data shows¶

    Does not support: We have no measurement on this point: citation decay. Study 3 is a registered protocol for release-to-release absence persistence and remains unrun until its comparability conditions are met. Vendor absence persistence is also a different event from a particular URL’s citation half-life.

    Supports: The September 2026 release supplies the answers for our repeated-question analysis. In answers captured on 22 and 23 September 2026, it observed 1,259 mixed-naming groups among 14,192 complete vendor-question-engine groups: 8.9%, Wilson 95% interval 8.4% to 9.4%. Mixed means named in one or two of three valid repeats. These within-release groups do not measure elapsed-time decay. See the measurement-noise finding and the Study 3 protocol.

    Suggests: Follow-up within the stated setting.

    What is citation decay?¶

    Citation decay is a decline in a defined page’s citation measure over comparable observations; a half-life requires an explicit baseline, threshold and time rule.

    Observed answers on stated dates, not a ranking. An old page that is cited today has not necessarily decayed. A previously cited page missing from a later answer may reflect ordinary answer variation. The term becomes useful when it names a measured change through time under a stated observation design.

    The practical reporting question belongs in the library’s historical data and time-series guidance. Here we define the event that a time series would need to establish.

    Where does the current AI-search usage come from?¶

    The earliest dated primary product explanation of the exact term we verified is Profound’s 29 September 2026 announcement by Joey Adelman and Matthew Huo. That is a bounded source finding, not a claim that no earlier author used the words in another field or on another site.

    Profound defines a page’s citation share against all citations across the models it tracks, smoothed over a two-week window. Its half-life runs from the page’s peak to half that peak, with a requirement to remain at or below the threshold for 14 consecutive days. These are Profound’s operational choices, not a universal definition imposed on other studies. [Adelman & Huo, 2026].

    The product also excludes pages that do not meet its age, citation-count and peak-activity rules. Consequently, a summary for eligible pages should not be generalized to every published URL. The vendor’s concept is useful precisely because it says which curve and which threshold it means.

    Choose the quantity before fitting a curve¶

    Absolute citation count, share of citations, proportion of answers citing a URL and proportion of questions ever citing it are different measures. A page can keep receiving the same number of citations while losing share because the rest of the observed citation pool grows.

    Specify the URL identity rule. A changed tracking parameter should not necessarily start a new page history, while a substantially revised document at a stable address may need a version label. Explain whether redirects, canonical declarations or a manually maintained document identifier connect observations.

    Define the observation window and treatment of missing collection. An unsuccessful capture is not an observed absence. A page that has not crossed the threshold by the last observation has an incomplete time-to-event record, not a measured infinite life or an invented future decay date.

    Why a missing citation is weak evidence by itself¶

    Generated answers can differ under repeated questions. A before/after disappearance might therefore be a transient answer change rather than a durable loss. Repetitions help reveal that variation, while a stable comparison set helps separate page-specific changes from broader engine or collection changes.

    Do not select a peak retrospectively and then describe every ordinary fluctuation below it as deterioration. State whether the peak is defined across the whole observed series, within a moving window or from an initial baseline. Different definitions can produce different half-lives from the same records.

    Calendar age also differs from time since first observed citation. A document may have existed for years before entering the tracked question set. Without earlier observations, “first cited” means first seen by that collection, not necessarily the first citation anywhere.

    Can decay justify a content refresh?¶

    A declining series can identify a page worth investigating. It does not establish that rewriting it will recover citations. Check whether the facts became stale, the question set changed, a competing source appeared, or the engine changed its source presentation.

    If an intervention follows, record its date and preserve the earlier version. Report the outcome against an appropriate comparison design. A refresh recommendation and a demonstrated refresh effect are separate claims, and a decay estimate supplies only the former unless the later test supports more.

    Joey Adelman and Matthew Huo write, “We track this on a rolling two-week average”. That smoothing choice is part of Profound’s published product definition, rather than a rule established for every citation dataset. [Adelman and Huo, 29 September 2026, “What Citation Decay shows”; verified 30 October 2026].

    You can distinguish an ageing document from a measured decline in citation share.

    What our own data shows¶

    Does not support: We have no measurement on this point: citation decay. Study 3 is a registered protocol for release-to-release absence persistence and remains unrun until its comparability conditions are met. Vendor absence persistence is also a different event from a particular URL’s citation half-life.

    Supports: The September 2026 release supplies the answers for our repeated-question analysis. It observed 1,259 mixed-naming groups among 14,192 complete vendor-question-engine groups: 8.9%, Wilson 95% interval 8.4% to 9.4%. Mixed means named in one or two of three valid repeats. These within-release groups do not measure elapsed-time decay. See the measurement-noise finding and the Study 3 protocol.

    Suggests: Follow-up within the stated setting.

Observed answers on stated dates, not a ranking.

    Synthetic audit example, Northstar Lab (retired Category Audit format)¶

    This synthetic example uses the retired Category Audit format for orders before 26 October 2026.

    ResourcesEight playbooksFictional AuditRecorded demosSources

    Synthetic learning example , not a client result or live AI measurement. Prepared 2026-09-24; version bw-content-2026-09-24-v1. No client, live engine, payment or delivered engagement is represented. Scenario timestamps are authored fixture metadata.

    Executive decision

    Fictional buyer: a small laboratory evaluating formulation-record software. The strongest supported issue is a contradiction between the exercise integration draft and its product sheet. Prepare a bounded clarification of connector type and edition requirements. No observation establishes that this wording caused an absence, that any real engine would respond differently, or that a sale was lost.

    Priority order: DEMO-WO-01 fixes the direct integration contradiction; DEMO-WO-02 adds missing prerequisites; DEMO-WO-03 prepares a source-name correction for later authorized review. Implementation and any live review session are separate unless expressly included in the actual engagement. No purchase is justified by these fictional measurements.

    Actual fixture coverage

    Six authored observation slots; three completed; one failed; one untested; one uncertain. Of the completed records, one has a reviewed present mention, one a reviewed absent mention and one awaits classification. The reviewed mention denominator is two. This small synthetic set has no population, independent-buyer or real performance interpretation.

    All records use engine fictional-test-surface, interface local-fixture, provider null, method synthetic-example-v1. Locale context: en-US fictional exercise; times are fixture metadata on September 24, 2026. No provider calls ran. The question IDs and receipt IDs are preserved in the exact JSON appendix. This six-slot teaching fixture does not replace any contracted Audit measurement allowance.

    What the evidence supports

    Finding F-01: DEMO-RECEIPT-001 names Northstar Lab and describes connector-based export. That is a present mention, not a recommendation. Separately DEMO-PAGE-01 says native on every plan, while DEMO-FACT-01/02 state third-party connector, Team edition and separate account. This independent conflict supports reviewing the draft wording; it does not establish a ranking cause.

    Finding F-02: DEMO-RECEIPT-002 omits the current and former fictional names in a completed reviewed answer about migration. No cause is known. DEMO-PAGE-02 separately omits edition/account prerequisites supplied by DEMO-FACT-02. Missing page detail is distinguished from a false statement.

    Finding F-03: DEMO-PAGE-03 uses the former name as current, while DEMO-FACT-03 distinguishes them. A correction draft is supported. No request was sent and no listing changed. Historical records retain their original names.

    Three implementation-ready proposals

    DEMO-WO-01 , Clarify third-party integration scope (P1)

    Direct contradiction could misstate compatibility and edition fit.

    Affected fixture URL: https://example.com/demo/integrations/atlas. Evidence: DEMO-PAGE-01, DEMO-FACT-01, DEMO-FACT-02.

    Proposed change: Replace the unsupported draft with: “Export to Atlas Analytics through the third-party BridgeKit connector. Requires Northstar Lab Team edition and a separately configured BridgeKit account. Confirm the documented prerequisites before setup.” Link the approved exercise product sheet; do not state a price or activation time.

    Scope: One integration paragraph and its duplicated on-page summary; no connector implementation or new page allowance.

    Dependencies: Current approved product fact version; Authorized page owner and scoped allowance; Existing release path and preview.

    Recommended role: Product content editor; technical/product reviewer. Real owner, approver and due date remain unassigned.

    Acceptance:

    • Native and every-plan claims removed from the scoped paragraph and its duplicated summary.
    • Connector type, Team edition and separate account prerequisite visible together.
    • Source version DEMO-DOC-01 is linked in the implementation record; fictional product reviewer role checks every factual clause.
    • Keyboard-accessible source link; no overflow at 360, 768 and 1440 pixels.
    • Fictional status remains in the page preview and export.

    Recheck: After actual publication evidence, product approval and a separately authorized matching question/method recheck.

    Rollback: Restore only the changed paragraph from the owner-recorded previous page revision. Preserve legitimate unrelated changes.

    DEMO-WO-02 , State edition and account prerequisites (P2)

    Missing prerequisites can leave an evaluator unable to assess edition fit; no contradictory price is established.

    Affected fixture URL: https://example.com/demo/editions. Evidence: DEMO-PAGE-02, DEMO-FACT-02.

    Proposed change: Add below the BridgeKit export description: “Available for Northstar Lab Team edition in this fictional catalogue. A separately configured BridgeKit account is required. Price and setup timing are not specified in this exercise; confirm current terms before deciding.” Preserve all existing price and contract fields.

    Scope: One explanatory block; no price, contract, credit, guarantee or purchased allowance change.

    Dependencies: DEMO-FACT-02; Unchanged current commercial record; Page owner review.

    Recommended role: Product content editor; commercial reviewer. Real owner, approver and due date remain unassigned.

    Acceptance:

    • Edition and account dependency are stated beside export wording.
    • No added numeric price, discount, guarantee or timing promise.
    • Unknown price and timing remain unknown; commercial reviewer approval required before real adaptation.
    • Existing commercial fields preserved in diff; source and synthetic labels retained.

    Recheck: Only after the edition block is publicly accessible and relevant comparable scope is approved.

    Rollback: Revert the bounded explanatory block using the recorded prior page revision.

    DEMO-WO-03 , Prepare a current-name correction (P3)

    Independent listing name conflict is supported, but a third-party change depends on its owner.

    Affected fixture URL: https://example.com/demo/directory/northstar. Evidence: DEMO-PAGE-03, DEMO-FACT-03.

    Proposed change: Prepare only this correction draft for the authorized source owner: “The current fictional product name is Northstar Lab. Northstar Notes is the former name. Please update the current-name field while retaining historical references where relevant. Supporting exercise evidence: DEMO-DOC-02.” Do not send or alter the external listing.

    Scope: One correction draft; no sending from this lane, paid placement, review campaign or promised acceptance.

    Dependencies: Current-name approval; Verified recipient and authority; Explicit send authorization under the actual project.

    Recommended role: Authorized source-correction owner; product reviewer. Real owner, approver and due date remain unassigned.

    Acceptance:

    • Exact current-name field identified; source supports current and former names.
    • Draft distinguishes requested update, submission and actual source change.
    • No invented recipient, impersonation, paid placement or review request.
    • Authorized sender and recipient remain unconfirmed until the real project owner verifies them.
    • Historical receipts unchanged; synthetic labels retained.

    Recheck: Only when the actual listing change is verified; a sent request alone is insufficient.

    Rollback: Draft can be withdrawn locally. A submitted request has no assumed reverse action; reconcile with source owner.

    Next decision and uncertainty

    This is a teaching package, so it creates no commercial obligation or measured business result. In a real Audit, proceed only if independently supported work is useful to the buyer and falls within an approved scope. Otherwise refine questions, gather missing evidence or recommend no additional purchase. The follow-up fixture illustrates no mention improvement in one matched pair and a failed follow-up in another; neither is hidden.

Synthetic learning example , not a client result or live AI measurement. Prepared 2026-09-24; version bw-content-2026-09-24-v1. No client, live engine, payment or delivered engagement is represented. Scenario timestamps are authored fixture metadata.

Executive decision

Fictional buyer: a small laboratory evaluating formulation-record software. The strongest supported issue is a contradiction between the exercise integration draft and its product sheet. Prepare a bounded clarification of connector type and edition requirements. No observation establishes that this wording caused an absence, that any real engine would respond differently, or that a sale was lost.

Priority order: DEMO-WO-01 fixes the direct integration contradiction; DEMO-WO-02 adds missing prerequisites; DEMO-WO-03 prepares a source-name correction for later authorized review. Implementation and any live review session are separate unless expressly included in the actual engagement. No purchase is justified by these fictional measurements.

Actual fixture coverage

Six authored observation slots; three completed; one failed; one untested; one uncertain. Of the completed records, one has a reviewed present mention, one a reviewed absent mention and one awaits classification. The reviewed mention denominator is two. This small synthetic set has no population, independent-buyer or real performance interpretation.

All records use engine fictional-test-surface, interface local-fixture, provider null, method synthetic-example-v1. Locale context: en-US fictional exercise; times are fixture metadata on September 24, 2026. No provider calls ran. The question IDs and receipt IDs are preserved in the exact JSON appendix. This six-slot teaching fixture does not replace any contracted Audit measurement allowance.

What the evidence supports

Finding F-01: DEMO-RECEIPT-001 names Northstar Lab and describes connector-based export. That is a present mention, not a recommendation. Separately DEMO-PAGE-01 says native on every plan, while DEMO-FACT-01/02 state third-party connector, Team edition and separate account. This independent conflict supports reviewing the draft wording; it does not establish a ranking cause.

Finding F-02: DEMO-RECEIPT-002 omits the current and former fictional names in a completed reviewed answer about migration. No cause is known. DEMO-PAGE-02 separately omits edition/account prerequisites supplied by DEMO-FACT-02. Missing page detail is distinguished from a false statement.

Finding F-03: DEMO-PAGE-03 uses the former name as current, while DEMO-FACT-03 distinguishes them. A correction draft is supported. No request was sent and no listing changed. Historical records retain their original names.

Three implementation-ready proposals

DEMO-WO-01 , Clarify third-party integration scope (P1)

Direct contradiction could misstate compatibility and edition fit.

Affected fixture URL: https://example.com/demo/integrations/atlas. Evidence: DEMO-PAGE-01, DEMO-FACT-01, DEMO-FACT-02.

Proposed change: Replace the unsupported draft with: “Export to Atlas Analytics through the third-party BridgeKit connector. Requires Northstar Lab Team edition and a separately configured BridgeKit account. Confirm the documented prerequisites before setup.” Link the approved exercise product sheet; do not state a price or activation time.

Scope: One integration paragraph and its duplicated on-page summary; no connector implementation or new page allowance.

Dependencies: Current approved product fact version; Authorized page owner and scoped allowance; Existing release path and preview.

Recommended role: Product content editor; technical/product reviewer. Real owner, approver and due date remain unassigned.

Acceptance:

  • Native and every-plan claims removed from the scoped paragraph and its duplicated summary.
  • Connector type, Team edition and separate account prerequisite visible together.
  • Source version DEMO-DOC-01 is linked in the implementation record; fictional product reviewer role checks every factual clause.
  • Keyboard-accessible source link; no overflow at 360, 768 and 1440 pixels.
  • Fictional status remains in the page preview and export.

Recheck: After actual publication evidence, product approval and a separately authorized matching question/method recheck.

Rollback: Restore only the changed paragraph from the owner-recorded previous page revision. Preserve legitimate unrelated changes.

DEMO-WO-02 , State edition and account prerequisites (P2)

Missing prerequisites can leave an evaluator unable to assess edition fit; no contradictory price is established.

Affected fixture URL: https://example.com/demo/editions. Evidence: DEMO-PAGE-02, DEMO-FACT-02.

Proposed change: Add below the BridgeKit export description: “Available for Northstar Lab Team edition in this fictional catalogue. A separately configured BridgeKit account is required. Price and setup timing are not specified in this exercise; confirm current terms before deciding.” Preserve all existing price and contract fields.

Scope: One explanatory block; no price, contract, credit, guarantee or purchased allowance change.

Dependencies: DEMO-FACT-02; Unchanged current commercial record; Page owner review.

Recommended role: Product content editor; commercial reviewer. Real owner, approver and due date remain unassigned.

Acceptance:

  • Edition and account dependency are stated beside export wording.
  • No added numeric price, discount, guarantee or timing promise.
  • Unknown price and timing remain unknown; commercial reviewer approval required before real adaptation.
  • Existing commercial fields preserved in diff; source and synthetic labels retained.

Recheck: Only after the edition block is publicly accessible and relevant comparable scope is approved.

Rollback: Revert the bounded explanatory block using the recorded prior page revision.

DEMO-WO-03 , Prepare a current-name correction (P3)

Independent listing name conflict is supported, but a third-party change depends on its owner.

Affected fixture URL: https://example.com/demo/directory/northstar. Evidence: DEMO-PAGE-03, DEMO-FACT-03.

Proposed change: Prepare only this correction draft for the authorized source owner: “The current fictional product name is Northstar Lab. Northstar Notes is the former name. Please update the current-name field while retaining historical references where relevant. Supporting exercise evidence: DEMO-DOC-02.” Do not send or alter the external listing.

Scope: One correction draft; no sending from this lane, paid placement, review campaign or promised acceptance.

Dependencies: Current-name approval; Verified recipient and authority; Explicit send authorization under the actual project.

Recommended role: Authorized source-correction owner; product reviewer. Real owner, approver and due date remain unassigned.

Acceptance:

  • Exact current-name field identified; source supports current and former names.
  • Draft distinguishes requested update, submission and actual source change.
  • No invented recipient, impersonation, paid placement or review request.
  • Authorized sender and recipient remain unconfirmed until the real project owner verifies them.
  • Historical receipts unchanged; synthetic labels retained.

Recheck: Only when the actual listing change is verified; a sent request alone is insufficient.

Rollback: Draft can be withdrawn locally. A submitted request has no assumed reverse action; reconcile with source owner.

Next decision and uncertainty

This is a teaching package, so it creates no commercial obligation or measured business result. In a real Audit, proceed only if independently supported work is useful to the buyer and falls within an approved scope. Otherwise refine questions, gather missing evidence or recommend no additional purchase. The follow-up fixture illustrates no mention improvement in one matched pair and a failed follow-up in another; neither is hidden.

Inspect the exact evidence

  • Observation export
  • Receipt text and review
  • Synthetic approved facts
  • Independent synthetic source passages
  • Three work orders
  • Scope, dependencies, priorities and rollback
  • No-improvement recheck example
  • Inspect the baseline and follow-up receipt bodies
  • Reusable executive template

Review and delivery state

This fictional teaching example does not represent a delivered client Audit. Its source records are available above; no live provider calls or client access are involved. Human review: not recorded.
